subject: dec
title: DEC.------C.CONT.
description: Diagram in AF(D)-15 (Affinity Dynamics, Level One) accompanying Braxton's analysis of redocumentation: 'the inability of given groups to acknowledge the dynamic offerings of another group (or the seriousness of time change, as a factor that promotes memory gaps) can better help us to understand what has happened to make this cycle as it is.' (C)DEC (the concept of decision) is crossed with C-CONT (composite continuance): the question is what decision produces when crossed with composite-continuance — decision being the act of acknowledgment-or-suppression that determines whether transferred information continues honestly. MT-INFO (multi-information) sits at the upper-right of the partner. INFO-DY (information dynamics) anchors the right output. INFO-COMP (information composite) sits between subject and partner as central hub. (R)PART (the reality of participation) hangs on the right output. PR-TR (principal transformation) sits below the crossing. EXP-F (experimental functionalism) anchors the lower-center. POL-P (political particulars), AS-ES (aspect essence), DYM-F (dynamics fundamentals), and UNF-PI (unified principle information) form the lower upstream cluster. Structural argument: decision crossed with composite-continuance is mediated by information-composite as central hub. The lower upstreams — political-particulars, aspect-essence, dynamics-fundamentals, unified-principle-information — show Braxton's commitment to a *quadrupled* lower upstream, an unusually strong decentralization signal: composite-continuance can only emerge through decision when at least four distinct lower considerations are live. The diagram exposes that memory-gap (the cycle's pathology) results when decision is taken without these four upstream tests.
